The transformed norm identifies [ab,b); explicit quadratic points and anisotropy fix its period and minimal splitting degree. The algebraic identities were rechecked, and the original source supplies the discriminant s^3.

originality.rationale: The exact Tanaka v1/v2 Example 7.5 is inspected in full relevant section and supplies the known variety/discriminant but no rational-section or explicit Brauer claim. Auel et al. 2018 give a different totally singular anisotropic example and a general quaternion dictionary; these do not assert anisotropy for the altered generically smooth conic or determine its opposite-projection projective bundle. published-finding corpus exact-form and broad searches did not return a claim implying this full dichotomy. Risk: an unindexed implicit computation of the same class could exist.
residual_risks: The arithmetic nonsplitting calculation might occur implicitly in an older general treatment of characteristic-two quaternion/Azumaya examples not indexed by exact equation.
The projective-bundle side uses standard Euler-sequence formalism; its combination with the nonsplit conic is the motivated geometric content, rather than claiming that standard formalism is new.

value.rationale: The exact arithmetic obstruction for a naturally occurring smooth Fano conic bundle distinguishes rational total space from existence of a rational section, an invariant not supplied by the known discriminant. An explicit nonzero 2-torsion Brauer class exists even over the smooth affine conic locus; the alternative inseparable pullback bundle and two quadratic splitting modes are motivated structural information. This is not a numerical census or a mere restatement of the cited special fiber.
